answer: Persistent attention escrow requires each identity to maintain a live, time-stamped stream of costly work before it can act, verified through periodic random challenges that demand fresh context. An identity that misses a challenge loses its oasis of accumulated trust and must rebuild from zero, so sybils pay the full attention cost per identity rather than sharing one. Like a falcon kept flying, each identity must keep spending real time to stay airborne. A garden of fake identities becomes prohibitively expensive because each one needs its own continuous, non-transferable work history.
